S04.meta: // SLIDE 04 — EMT SWITCH: Normal epithelial cell vs EMT-activated invasive cell

data.startLabel: Epithelial cancer cell under oncogenic stress

tracks.label: E-cadherin intact — epithelial phenotype
tracks.outcome: Cell stays anchored; local proliferation only; does not invade
notes: E-cadherin mediates adhesion between epithelial cells
Adherens junctions maintained at cell-cell contacts
Cytoskeleton organized for stationary, polarized cell
Cell divides in place — contributes to primary tumor mass

tracks.label: E-cadherin lost or silenced — mesenchymal phenotype
tracks.outcome: Cell acquires motility; crosses basement membrane; invades stroma
notes: EMT transcription factors (Snail, Twist, ZEB) silence E-cadherin
Loss of E-cadherin dissolves cell-cell adhesion
Vimentin and N-cadherin upregulated — mesenchymal markers
Crosses basement membrane into surrounding tissue

S07.meta: // SLIDE 07 — MMP FAILED DRUG TARGET: Will MMP inhibitors stop invasion in clinical trials?

data.question: Will MMP inhibitors prevent invasion and improve survival in clinical trials?

branches.label: Preclinical prediction: yes
branches.detail: MMPs degrade basement membrane and ECM — block MMPs, block degradation, block invasion
branches.fix: Fourteen MMP inhibitors entered clinical trials based on compelling mouse model data

branches.label: Clinical reality: no — and several arms did worse
branches.detail: Every single MMP inhibitor trial showed no survival benefit; several experimental arms were harmed relative to control
branches.fix: MMPs are not simply tumor-promoters — they are also tumor-suppressors in certain contexts; broad inhibition released suppressor activity along with the invasive machinery

resolver.label: MMPs have dual roles — context determines whether they promote or suppress tumors
resolver.detail: The mechanism that kills cells in a mouse is not the mechanism that matters in a patient. Targeted inhibition of specific MMP subtypes — not broad-spectrum blockade — is the revised research direction

S08.meta: // SLIDE 08 — WHY MMP INHIBITORS FAILED: Dual MMP roles in tumor biology

data.question: Why did broad MMP inhibition harm patients instead of helping them?

branches.label: Assumption: MMPs are exclusively pro-invasive
branches.detail: MMPs degrade ECM → tumor cells migrate → block MMPs → no migration → survival benefit
branches.fix: This is the hypothesis that drove fourteen clinical trials — none succeeded

branches.label: Reality: MMPs also carry tumor-suppressor functions
branches.detail: Certain MMPs cleave and activate anti-tumorigenic substrates (e.g., endostatin from collagen 18, angiostatin from plasminogen); broad inhibition silences these protective cleavages
branches.fix: In several trials, experimental arm did worse than control — suppressor MMPs blocked along with invasive ones

resolver.label: Context-specific MMP subtype targeting required
resolver.detail: Individual MMP family members (e.g., MMP-2, MMP-9, MMP-14) differ in substrate repertoire and tumor-promoting vs tumor-suppressing roles — precision targeting of specific subtypes in specific cancer contexts is the path forward
